claims.claim: ⚠️ **The Sydney funnel-web can cause lethal envenoming**, though no severe envenoming has been recorded in Victoria despite some Victorian spiders having similar toxicity.
claims.source_text: Big black spiders include the Sydney Funnel Web, which can cause lethal envenoming, however there have not been any cases of severe envenoming in Victoria, despite some Victorian spiders having similar toxicity
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The Victorian funnel-web (Dandenong Ranges) is not significantly venomous** — bite-site pain, headache, nausea. **Beware collectors' Sydney funnel-webs**; other funnel-webs and mouse spiders reaching eastern Victoria may cause systemic symptoms.
claims.source_text: The Victorian Funnel Web spider, found in the Dandenong Ranges area, is not significantly venomous and causes minor symptoms such as bite-site pain, headache and nausea … Whilst Sydney Funnel Webs should not be found in Victoria, beware of collectors … Other funnel web spiders and mouse spiders have a distribution extending into Eastern Victoria and may cause systemic symptoms
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Apart from redbacks, other Victorian spiders need no medical intervention or observation unless infection develops.**
claims.source_text: Apart from Red back spiders, other Victorian spiders do not require medical intervention or observation unless infection develops
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess anyone in whom a Sydney funnel-web bite is possible, and any symptomatic patient.**
claims.source_text: Any patient in whom a Sydney Funnel Web spider bite is possible Any symptomatic patient
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Only a small number of bites cause systemic envenoming; if it comes, it develops over 10 minutes to 4 hours.** Bite marks are usually seen.
claims.source_text: Bite marks are usually seen Only a small number of bites develop systemic envenomation If systemic symptoms develop, they do so over 10 min - 4 hours
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Systemic features:** perioral tingling · headache, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain · salivation, piloerection, sweating, lacrimation · hypertension and tachycardia that may progress to bradycardia and hypotension · pulmonary oedema, cyanosis, respiratory failure.
claims.source_text: Perioral tingling Headache, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain Salivation, piloerection, sweating and lacrimation, due to autonomic hyperactivity Hypertension and tachycardia - may progress to bradycardia and hypotension Pulmonary oedema, cyanosis, respiratory failure
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Apply a pressure immobilisation bandage.** If history or examination suggests envenoming, **leave it on** and discuss with the Poisons Information Centre.
claims.source_text: Apply a pressure immobilisation bandage If history or examination findings suggest envenomation, leave bandage in place and discuss with the Poisons Information Centre
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No Victorian hospital stocks Sydney funnel-web antivenom** — contact the Poisons Information Centre. If a Sydney funnel-web is possible or the child is symptomatic, **obtain 4 ampoules of CSL funnel-web spider antivenom before removing the bandage.**
claims.source_text: Contact Poisons Information Centre (13 11 26) in Victoria as no hospitals stock Sydney Funnel Web antivenom … If Sydney Funnel Web is possible, or if symptomatic, obtain 4 ampoules of CSL funnel web spider antivenom before removing bandage
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Without antivenom, support organ by organ:** pulmonary oedema — intubation, IPPV/PEEP · hypertension and tachycardia — alpha blockade · hypotension — fluids, inotropes, atropine.
claims.source_text: In the absence of antivenom, management may require Pulmonary oedema - intubation, IPPV/ PEEP, Hypertension and tachycardia- sympathetic blockade (alpha) Hypotension - fluids, ionotropes, atropine
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Possible Sydney funnel-web, or any symptoms: discharge only if asymptomatic 4 hours after the bite and at least 2 hours after first aid is removed.**
claims.source_text: If Sydney funnel Web is possible, or if was symptomatic: discharge if asymptomatic at 4 hours post bite, at least 2 hours after removal of first aid.
